plan.contextChunk: This figure is a scene diagram of an airplane sighting two points on a straight highway below it. A small colored drawing of a jetliner sits at the upper left, nose pointed left, and a teal dashed horizontal line runs to the right from the aircraft to stand for the horizontal at flight altitude. Across the lower part of the figure a solid black horizontal line represents the highway, with two labeled points on it: A toward the middle and B at the far right. Two gray dashed sight lines drop from the airplane to those points, the line to A being the steeper of the pair and the line to B running much shallower because B lies farther off. Arcs drawn at the airplane mark the two angles opening downward from the dashed horizontal, labeled 25 degrees for the shallow line toward B and 49 degrees for the steep line toward A. Sharing a single vertex for both angles of depression turns the two sight lines and the road into a pair of triangles with a common side. The arrangement supports solving for the airplane's slant distance to A and its elevation above the road once the spacing between the two mileposts is supplied.

interactions.label: Airplane altitude
interactions.teaches: Raising or lowering the plane changes both depression angles together because tan(angle) = altitude / horizontal distance, so the altitude is the common vertical leg in both right triangles

interactions.label: Distance A–B
interactions.teaches: Sliding B along the road changes only the shallow angle to B while the altitude and the steep angle to A stay put, making the shared-altitude constraint that couples the two triangles visible

interactions.label: Solve
interactions.teaches: Stepping through the construction shows how the horizontal reference defines the depression angles, how a dropped perpendicular turns the scene into two right triangles sharing one altitude, and how the unknown slant distances and height then follow from the tangent and sine ratios

demo_steps.narration: The teal dashed line is the horizontal at flight altitude; each gray sight line opens downward from it, giving the 25° depression angle to B and the 49° depression angle to A from a single shared vertex.

demo_steps.title: Form the two right triangles
demo_steps.narration: Dropping a perpendicular from the plane to the road splits the scene into two right triangles that share the same vertical altitude leg — the steep triangle to A and the shallow triangle to B.

demo_steps.title: Reveal the unknown distances
demo_steps.narration: With the shared altitude linking the triangles, the tangent ratios give the horizontal distances and the sine ratios give the slant distances; drag the altitude or the A–B spacing to watch every labeled length and angle update consistently.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Both angles of depression hang off one horizontal at the plane, so the two sight-line triangles share a single vertical altitude — that common side is the bridge that turns two angles and one road spacing into a solvable system for height and slant range.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Place the airplane icon at the upper left with its nose pointing left; run a teal dashed horizontal line to the right from it as the altitude reference. Across the bottom draw a solid black highway line with point A near the middle and point B at the far right, each labeled. From the airplane draw two gray dashed sight lines, the steeper one to A and the shallower one to B. At the airplane vertex draw two concentric angle arcs opening downward from the horizontal, the inner labeled with the live shallow angle (≈25°) and the outer with the live steep angle (≈49°); these numbers must recompute as sliders move. In the 'Right triangles' phase add a vertical altitude segment from the plane straight down to the highway with a small right-angle square at the foot and horizontal distance ticks to A and to B. In the 'Reveal distances' phase annotate the altitude value and the two slant distances. Keep the airplane, road, and reference line fixed in position while the sight lines, arcs, and revealed segments respond to the sliders.

authoredContext:
A pilot is flying over a straight highway. He determines the angles of depression to two mileposts, 2.1 km apart, to be 25° and 49°, as shown in the figure. Find the distance of the plane from point A and the elevation of the plane.

Diagram of a plane flying over a highway. It is to the left and above points A and B on the ground in that order. There is a horizontal line going through the plan parallel to the ground. The angle formed by the horizontal line, the plane, and the line from the plane to point B is 25 degrees. The angle formed by the horizontal line, the plane, and point A is 49 degrees.
